introduction: The proposed review aims to investigate the effects of chronic exercise on overall depression severity and on different depressive symptoms in older adults with a mean age of at least 60, in randomized controlled trials. It will also consider how intervention and individual characteristics moderate these effects.
methodology: Protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials, following PRISMA-P. Several electronic databases will be searched from inception. Pairs of reviewers will select studies, extract data and assess quality. A random-effects model will be used, with Hedges’ g as the summary effect.
theory: The review organizes its moderators around the FITT principles of exercise training (frequency, intensity, time and type of exercise).
discussion: The authors expect a moderate exercise effect on depression, in line with earlier meta-analyses. They say the review may be the first to examine effects on different depressive symptoms across many moderators. Its conclusions may support individualized exercise recommendations and reveal research gaps.
limitations: The authors plan to exclude RCTs testing pharmacological treatment and/or psychotherapy, so no conclusions can be drawn for add-on treatment; they acknowledge possibly missing relevant insights. They anticipate heterogeneous data and varied reporting of exercise and individual characteristics.

limitations.q: We plan to exclude RCTs with tested effects of pharmacological treatment and / or psychotherapy. Therefore, no conclusions can be drawn for exercise interventions as add-on treatment.

abstract_claims.q: There is high evidence that chronic exercise benefits overall depression severity in older adults.
The results of the proposed review are anticipated to have a substantial impact on research and clinical practice.
On the one hand, the review’s conclusions could form the foundation for developing evidence-based recommendations for individualized exercise programs that alleviate depression in older adults
by revealing research gaps, the review results could encourage the formulation of research questions for further RCTs
